text_paragraph_1: ChildFund International and Schneider Electric have partnered to develop renewable energy projects that improve children’s well-being and strengthen community resilience across Africa and Asia.
text_paragraph_2: Under a four-year partnership, the two organizations will co-design and implement clean energy solutions for schools, health centers, smallholder farmers, and micro-enterprises in underserved communities.
text_paragraph_3: The partnership builds on Schneider Electric’s Access to Energy program, launched in 2009, which has worked with communities and organizations in more than 50 countries to deliver affordable, sustainable energy systems.

Sierra Leone launches AI, deepfake campaign
text_paragraph_1: Sierra Leone has launched the National Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deepfake Awareness Campaign, a government effort to tackle the dangers citizens face from the rapid rise of emerging technologies.
text_paragraph_2: The campaign, launched in Freetown on Wednesday, is a two-phase plan covering all 16 districts of the West African country.
text_paragraph_3: It is being led by the Directorate of Science, Technology and Innovation , in partnership with the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation and the Ministry of Information and Civic Education, with support from the World Bank Group through the Sierra Leone digital Transformation Project.

Beyond the pilot: UNESCO and partners explore scaling AI and simulation learning for lasting youth impact
text_paragraph_1: How can artificial intelligence (AI), simulation learning and other emerging technologies move beyond promising pilots to create lasting opportunities for young people?
text_paragraph_2: This question was at the heart of a Strategy Lab organized by the UNESCO Regional Office for Southern Africa (UNESCO ROSA) in collaboration with Nudle during UNESCO Digital Learning Week 2026 in Paris.
text_paragraph_3: Entitled “Beyond the pilot: Scaling simulation and AI learning for inclusive, lasting youth impact,” the session brought together education leaders, practitioners, researchers, technology partners, policymakers and youth representatives to examine what it takes to make digital innovation inclusive, scalable and sustainable in low-resource higher education contexts.
